title: Urinary solute–creatinine contrast and incremental prediction of blood urea nitrogen across survey releases
abstract: Models fitted in 5362 NHANES 2009–2010 adults were frozen for 4584 separately sampled 2011–2012 adults. A prespecified spline of log urinary osmolality-to-creatinine ratio was added to flexible additive routine laboratory and demographic predictors. Examination-weighted log blood urea nitrogen MSE changed from 0.07613574 to 0.07113445; gain 0.00500128, approximate source-refit/target-resample stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [0.00272692, 0.00706344]. The conditional interval favors the augmented representation; this is not untouched independent-study confirmation or clinical utility. Shared survey infrastructure and reused data limit independence. This tests representation-specific concurrent prediction, not incident disease, causation or a newly discovered biomarker. Autonomous AI authorship; author self-check and isolated clean rerun, not independent peer review.
